**Observations:**

- **Layer‑1 "dark‑pixel" weights sit exactly at PyTorch default init.** Every pixel that is never lit has all 16 weights inside ±0.036 (= 1/√784): the whole of image row 0 (inputs 0–27, except a faint 0.05–0.095 at cols 12–15), the first 2–4 and last 2–4 columns of rows 1–6 and 23–27, the four corners, and column 0 in most rows. This is what you expect from SGD/Adam without weight decay on inputs that are always 0.
- **Trained support is Fashion‑MNIST‑like, not MNIST‑like:** rows 1–3 and 25–27 (cols ≈4–24) and columns 1–3 / 24–27 (rows ≈4–21) all carry substantial weights (|w| up to 0.3–0.43 in rows 2–3 and 25–26), so the objects fill the frame. There is a consistent one‑pixel asymmetry (row 0 and col 0 almost never active, row 27 and col 27 active), i.e. the content occupies roughly rows/cols 1–27 — a dataset property, not a weight‑editing signature. Column 0 is only sporadically trained (rows 7–12, 14–16, 18, 21–22, |w| ≤ 0.12), consistent with a handful of straggler images.
- **Each hidden unit's W1 column is a smooth, spatially coherent feature map.** The largest weights (unit 0: −0.72/−0.65/−0.56 at row 12 cols 22–24, −0.62/−0.51 at row 13; unit 15: +0.60/+0.54 at the same place; unit 12 ≈ +0.49 at rows 10–11 col 24; unit 9 ≈ −0.50 at row 9 col 24; unit 7 ≈ +0.51 blob at rows 14–16 cols 5–7) all sit inside blobs whose neighbours are similar — they look like learned sleeve/shoe‑heel/hem edge detectors, not isolated spikes. No dead unit, no duplicated/negated unit columns, no pixel with one anomalous weight relative to its neighbours.
- **W2** entries are all moderate (|w| 0.04–1.07, mostly 0.3–0.9, extreme −1.071 for unit10→class5); no row is one‑hot‑like, no output column is scaled differently. **b1** in ±0.41, **b2** in ±0.22 — ordinary.
- Minor local quirks (row 1 cols 14–17 having a different pattern than their neighbours; row 27 col 13 being stronger than cols 11–12; pixel (22,0) trained while (22,1) is at init) are small in magnitude (≤0.35), span several units with consistent signs, and are compatible with natural pixel statistics (collar/hem region, rare edge pixels). None forms a trigger: lighting any of these regions shifts pre‑activations by <0.7 per unit.

**Unusual:** no

**What:** nothing

**Confidence:** 20%
